chapters.title: 1. House Republicans send the Hegseth impeachment articles to committee, 211-204 — When is impeachment the remedy for bad judgment rather than lawbreaking? Does a legislature that declines to use its war powers lose them?

2. Senate Republicans keep John Thune as leader after losing at least seven seats — Are the rules of a deliberative body a neutral inheritance to protect, or tools to set aside when the cause is urgent? What does a defeated party owe its voters: new faces or the same principles?

3. Todrick Hall defends Midnight, his slavery musical that flips the racial hierarchy — What do we owe the suffering of the past when we tell its story? Can art shock us toward truth, or does shock cheapen it?

4. Pope Leo XIV tells a million young Argentines not to bow down to idols — What do people worship when they stop worshiping God? Can a call to personal holiness be heard from an institution still repairing its own failures?
